subject: Biotechnology
title: Extended Shelf Life
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Extended Shelf Life.

hook.text: One-third of all food produced is wasted — extending shelf life with biotech could save billions of tons.

buildup.text: Arctic apples have the polyphenol oxidase gene silenced — they do not brown when cut, reducing consumer rejection.

discovery.text: Innate potatoes resist bruising and produce less acrylamide when fried — safer and longer-lasting.

twist.text: These crops use gene silencing of existing genes — no foreign DNA, making regulatory approval easier.

climax.text: CRISPR-edited tomatoes with delayed ripening stay firm longer — reducing losses during transport and storage.

punchline.text: Slow the rot, cut the waste — biotech shelf life saves food and money.

quiz.question: How do Arctic apples prevent browning?
options: They are coated with a special wax after harvest
The polyphenol oxidase gene is silenced so the browning enzyme is not produced
They contain extra antioxidants that absorb oxygen
